t.t: Bring access management into one clear system.

SmartphoneKey connects the work of managing sites, people, credentials and supported devices. The Admin Panel is the place to organise that work; readers and connected devices carry it into the building.

div.p: Group the people and devices that belong to a customer installation. Use the site's context to review access and assign local management responsibilities.
Each site is organised as an Entity in the Admin Panel.
Add a person, assign the required credentials, review activity and change access when their needs change. For a disconnected device, some changes may remain pending until it reconnects.

Manage access as people and responsibilities change.
Organise sites, manage physical and supported digital credentials, and give the right people responsibility for day-to-day operations.

div.p: Find a customer installation and review its users, keys, locks and related devices. Keep separate buildings organised within the supported site hierarchy.
Give local administrators access to the areas they manage. Screens and actions depend on the person's permissions and subscription configuration.
Issue supported wallet credentials, manage physical cards and use supported temporary-access workflows. When access is no longer needed, revoke it and follow the delivery status.

A contractor needs access to a service area. The administrator selects the correct site and doors, issues the supported credential, and reviews its status. When the work ends, the administrator revokes access and checks the result.

Review activity and audit records. Use supported device monitoring to identify connectivity problems and failed operations. Alerts require configuration; they do not replace an agreed support process.
Some key changes are queued for later delivery. “Pending” means the change has not yet been confirmed on the device. Local credential behaviour depends on the device and configuration.
A revocation made while the reader is offline is not enforced until the reader confirms it.

section.h2: Check the capabilities behind the example.

div.p: A Matter label does not mean every device exposes the same commands. Scenarios depend on the commissioned devices, their reported capabilities and firmware. In the current implementation, each scenario belongs to one hub.

The management workflow distinguishes changes waiting for the hub from changes the hub has applied or rejected. Editing a scenario does not automatically replace the version already running on the hub.

section.h2: Explore AI Concierge for your site.

div.p: AI Concierge is designed to help interpret a visitor's request and work with configured access rules. Ask about the version and availability appropriate to your site.
AI Concierge features and rollout status vary by deployment. Confirm availability and the required setup with our team.
The v2 design uses AI to interpret the request and server-side rules to decide whether it can proceed. Do not interpret a convincing conversation as a permission grant.
If you cannot complete the guest flow, use the site's provided resident or support contact. The marketing site is not an emergency service or a live door-control interface.

t.t: Read the guidance, then ask about the visitor workflow and AI Concierge availability for your site.
